source_review.notes: Checked all twelve structured references. Current Kubernetes workload and pod-lifecycle documentation supports pod phases, conditions, container states, restart, termination, stop signals, and controller selection. Current probe guidance supports distinct startup, readiness, and liveness behavior and cascading-failure cautions. Current Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, and CronJob documentation supports identity, rollout, ordering, node coverage, completion, retries, scheduling, concurrency, and cleanup semantics. Current init/sidecar documentation supports startup, resource, probe, Job, and termination behavior. Current disruption and topology-spread guidance supports PDB scope, voluntary/involuntary disruptions, Eviction API, domain skew, selector, and capacity limitations. No source is treated as proof of application availability, data safety, exactly-once effects, or universal version behavior.

evidence: Checked W=(J,I,C,P,H,U,D,T,E,X), N/S/U rollout variables, pod owner/revision/readiness/availability/deletion functions, Job attempt set B_k, indicator sum, and topology-domain skew.
Checked tuple, set, indexed sum, indicator, implication, inequality, maximum/minimum, and time-function syntax with the repository GitHub-math validator.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Pod readiness, controller availability, finite-work completion, and business effect uniqueness remain distinct.

evidence: Executed workload-rollout-inventory and reproduced seven pods, six owned, four current revision, three updated-ready, one old-ready, one terminating, one orphan, and four serving candidates.
Recomputed ownership by deploy-u1; current revision pods are api-a through api-d, serving candidates are a/b/c and old, while drain is deleting and orphan is unowned.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The synthetic serving-candidate classification disclaims EndpointSlice, minimum-ready, reachability, correctness, and user-outcome equivalence.

evidence: Expanded the ten-element workload contract through semantics, identity, controller, placement, composition, update, disruption, termination, evidence, and exception sections.
Checked N+S transient rollout count and N-U availability target as controller bounds subject to rounding/current semantics rather than unconditional capacity guarantees.
Checked availability as stronger controller evidence than readiness while keeping both weaker than business success.
Checked successful Job exit existentially over attempts and verified that it does not imply exactly-once external effect.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The notation models workload constraints and evidence boundaries; it does not prove availability or effect uniqueness.

evidence: Reviewed bare/orphan pods, selector overlap/adoption, namesake UIDs, terminating lag, stale revision status, sidecar/init failure, ephemeral-debug authority, and probe dependency amplification.
Reviewed insufficient surge/quota/topology capacity, slow pull/start/warmup/drain, failed canary, mixed-version incompatibility, stalled progress, unsafe rollback, and force deletion.

Reviewed StatefulSet partition/node loss/duplicate member/storage reattachment, DaemonSet impaired-node placement and privilege, Job duplicate/unknown effects/poison inputs, and CronJob late/overlapping/replaced executions.
Reviewed PDB selector errors, direct deletion bypass, concurrent involuntary loss, unhealthy eviction, maintenance deadlock, incomplete topology labels, scale-to-zero domains, and scheduling skew.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Identity, lifecycle, rollout, completion, disruption, placement, and recovery remain explicit under normal and adversarial conditions.

evidence: Traced controller selection from job semantics through pod identity/composition, selector/ownership, probes, placement, rollout/completion, disruption, termination, and outcome evidence.
Checked no unmanaged application pods, disjoint selectors, disposable pod identity, distinct init/sidecar/app/debug roles, and separate startup/readiness/liveness questions.

Checked feasible rollout budgets, idempotent or deduplicated finite work, bounded PDB claims, measured graceful termination, and status interpretation through owner/revision/generation/pod/container/application evidence.
invariant_checking.notes: All declared workload, identity, probe, rollout, completion, disruption, termination, and evidence invariants hold across examples and answers.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states no theorem and contains no deductive proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; controller and application guarantees are explicitly conditional.

evidence: The executable rollout inventory is labeled synthetic and disclaims service and controller equivalence.
Current project documentation and practitioner synthesis remain distinguishable.
Worked examples are scenarios rather than production availability, performance, or security measurements.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external workload review, chaos test, rollout audit, benchmark, or production incident analysis is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently chooses controllers from replaceability, stable identity, node locality, finite completion, and schedule semantics, while separating pod state, controller evidence, disruption, and business outcome.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can select workload controllers, design pod/container lifecycle, probe contracts, Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet policies, Job/CronJob idempotency, placement, PDBs, termination, rollout compatibility, hierarchy observation, and failure tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence progresses from pod state and composition through each controller, placement, disruption, termination, rollout, observation, and testing. Ten examples remain distinct; five exercises progress from controller selection through rollout, diagnosis, batch scheduling, and robotics transfer, with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
